title: Your Blinker Won't Save You From a Charging Bison
description:
Your blinker won't save you from a charging bison. The polite-driver test, settled by a 2,000 pound animal.

The useless facts:
- Male bison can weigh up to 2,000 pounds, according to the National Park Service.
- Bison can run up to 35 miles per hour.
- Use your blinker anyway. The bison does.

Useless Facts is our series of true facts nobody needed. Be honest: do you signal every lane change?

Sources:
- National Park Service, Yellowstone: Bison (males up to 2,000 lb; can run up to 35 mph): https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/bison.htm
- National Park Service, Bison bison (biology, weight and speed): https://www.nps.gov/subjects/bison/index.htm

questions.q: How fast can a bison run?
questions.a: Bison can run up to 35 miles per hour, according to the National Park Service.

questions.q: How much does a bison weigh?
questions.a: Male bison can weigh up to 2,000 pounds; females are smaller, around 1,000 pounds.
Bison can charge when people get too close; Yellowstone asks visitors to stay at least 25 yards away and stay in their vehicles.
